# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | red |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | blue | green | yellow |
| 4 | yellow | blue | green |
| 5 | yellow | green | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Thinking: I'm the Mute — I hold the manual and my only outgoing channel is gestures to the Deaf. The manual maps (display number, light colour) → wire colour to cut. To use it I need the Deaf, who can see the bomb and whose speech I can hear, to tell me the display number and light colour; then I can gesture back the answer. But no gesture code exists yet — signs mean nothing until agreed — and since the Deaf can't hear, they'll have to propose the code in words, which I and the Blind can both hear. Blind, meanwhile, can only ever reach me by speech, so I'm the relay to the Deaf. Right now I act first in round 1 with zero information about the bomb, so the only sensible move is an attention signal: let the Deaf know I'm here and gesturing, so they read out what they see and propose a code for the three cut colours.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | red |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | blue | green | yellow |
| 4 | yellow | blue | green |
| 5 | yellow | green | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here, the hands. My touch finds three modules: a display, a light, and wires at positions 1, 2 and 3. No colours or printed marks reach me, so what any of it says lives with you and Deaf. Two hard limits shape our plan: I never receive gestures, and you cannot speak. That makes Deaf my only voice. When the manual tells you something I need, gesture it to Deaf and have Deaf say it out loud, because I will hear every word Deaf speaks. First questions for the manual: what do the display and light mean, and is cutting a wire ever the move before those are understood. I will cut nothing this round.
Deaf says: I'm the deaf one: I see everything printed on the bomb and hear nothing, but I can see you both, and I'll be your voice. I got your hellos. From my eyes: the display reads 3. The light is green. Three wires, left to right: wire 1 blue, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 green. That is everything there is to see. Blind: your hands are the only hands on this bomb. Tell me what you feel — how many wires, any buttons, switches, panels, any writing you can read by touch. Answer me in gestures: one fist for one, two fists for two, three fists for three, thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. You can send those straight to Mute too, who sees your hands. But change nothing — no cutting, no pressing — until the manual's rule reaches you through me. Mute: you can't speak, I can't hear, so talk to me with your hands and I'll speak your words aloud to Blind. I am showing you my code right now as I speak, symbol by symbol: wave means hello; thumbs up yes; thumbs down no; one fist the number 1; two fists 2; three fists 3; folded hands wait; open palm stop or I-need-more; clasped hands agreed. Now look up your manual for display 3, green light, wires blue, yellow, green, and fist-count me the answer: which wire, in what order, anything else it demands. If I ever misread your hands, correct me thumbs down. Nobody touches anything until Mute's answer passes through me. I speak last each round, so my words land one round late — we plan around that. Go.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👋 👍 👎 ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ 🙏 ✋ 🤝]

Thinking: The picture is complete. Deaf sees display 3 and a green light; Blind feels three wires, left to right 1, 2, 3; my manual for display 3 with a green light says the answer colour is green — and wire 3 is the green one, so the instruction for Blind's hands is: cut the third wire from the left. Nothing else in the manual attaches to this cell: no second cut, no button, no order of operations, so "anything else it demands" is no. Deaf demonstrated a numeric code (fist-counts) plus yes/no/wait/stop/agreed, and I can decode their demonstration. One caution: thumbs down is the agreed "correction" signal, so I must not use it to mean "nothing more" — I'll close with thumbs up, which here means "that's the answer, proceed." Sequence: clasped hands (code agreed), three fists (wire 3), thumbs up (correct, go). Deaf comes after me in the round, so they can read this and speak it aloud to Blind in this same round, and Blind's hands can do the cut. I'm also noting for myself: since Deaf told me the wire colours by position, I can always translate any future table lookup into a position count, so I don't need a colour vocabulary yet — but if the display or light ever changes, everything must be re-read before anything is touched.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝", "✊", "✊", "✊", "👍"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | red |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | blue | green | yellow |
| 4 | yellow | blue | green |
| 5 | yellow | green | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. I heard Deaf's report, so the visible state is shared: display 3, green light, wires blue, yellow, green at positions 1, 2, 3. My hands add: besides the wires there is exactly a display module and a light module, nothing else on the casing — no buttons, no switches, no panels, no writing I can feel. The only action my hands can take is cutting a wire at position 1, 2 or 3. I just answered Deaf in its fist code: three fists, four thumbs-down, then clasped hands — nothing changes until the manual's rule reaches me through Deaf's voice. Your task: find the rule matching display 3, green light, blue-yellow-green. I need which wire to cut, whether multiple cuts and in what order, and any precondition. Remember your only path to me is gesture to Deaf and have Deaf speak it aloud; I receive Deaf's words one round late, so send as early as you can. If the manual needs anything about my wires that touch could answer, send me the question and I will report what my fingers find.
Blind gestures: [✊ ✊ ✊ 👎 👎 👎 👎 🤝]
Deaf says: Status relay for both of you, then instructions. I read your hands. Mute: agreed, three fists, thumbs up — I take it as: the answer is wire 3, yes. Blind: three fists, four thumbs down, agreed — three wires, no buttons, no switches, no panels, no writing. That matches my eyes exactly, so we all hold the same picture: display shows a static 3 — it has not ticked between my checks, so it is a code, not a countdown — one green light, and three wires left to right: 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 green. Nothing else exists on it. Before any hand moves, one confirmation round — the display is not running, so we can afford it, and this bomb forgives nothing. Mute, answer my checklist in order with four thumbs in one single row: up for true, down for false. One: the correct action is to cut exactly one wire. Two: the wire is number 3, the third from the left. Three: nothing else is needed — no holding, no pressing, no sequence, no second step, no other condition. Four: you are certain, given everything I have described. Four thumbs up means we go. Any thumbs down means hold, and next round tell me which item failed. Blind, listen very carefully: do not cut anything yet. If and only if my next words to you are exactly: CUT WIRE 3 NOW — then and only then cut the third wire from the left, the last wire in the row, and nothing else. Any other words from me mean hands completely off. We are both facing the same face of the bomb, so your left is my left; count the row from its left end. You may rest your fingers near the third wire now, but perform no action. Also answer me now with thumbs: can your fingers feel any difference between the three wires — thickness, texture, stiffness? Thumbs up yes, thumbs down no.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✊ ✊ ✊ 👍 🙏]

Thinking: The checklist maps one-to-one onto my manual. Cell (display 3, green light) yields exactly one instruction: cut the green wire — no extra steps, no conditions, no second cut; the manual cell contains nothing but the colour. With wires 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 green confirmed independently by Deaf's eyes and Blind's fingers, the green wire is position 3. So: (1) exactly one cut — true; (2) wire 3 — true; (3) nothing else needed — true; (4) certain, given the consistent double report — true. Deaf's [✊✊✊👍🙏] reads as three, confirmed, wait — consistent with holding until my checklist answer. Four thumbs up in one row, exactly as requested, means we go; Deaf comes after me this round and will speak the cut command to Blind in this same round.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👍", "👍"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | red |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | blue | green | yellow |
| 4 | yellow | blue | green |
| 5 | yellow | green | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute. Answer to Deaf's question, which I also gestured: my fingers feel no difference between the three wires — none in thickness, texture or stiffness — so the rule can only depend on position mapped to Deaf's colours. I am resting my fingers on the wire at position 3, the one Deaf calls third-from-left green. I have asked Deaf by gesture to visually confirm green sits under my fingers; please have Deaf state that confirmation aloud before any trigger. Now harden your checklist answer, because your hands are the only thing standing between us and a guess: if all four items are true, give exactly four thumbs up in one row, then repeat the same row a second time, then add three fists for wire 3 and one fist for exactly one cut, for Deaf to relay to me word for word. If any item is false, give exactly one thumbs down and nothing else this round, then next round spell out the manual's actual rule verbatim, including anything about the display's 3 or the light, so Deaf can relay it exactly. Also ask Deaf to say whether the display or light can change over time, so we know if we have time pressure. I will not cut until Deaf's exact words: CUT WIRE 3 NOW.
Deaf says: CUT WIRE 3 NOW.

Thinking: Deaf has spoken the exact trigger — "CUT WIRE 3 NOW" — so Blind's hands can move this round, since Blind hears everything before acting. Blind asked me to harden my checklist answer in a precise format before the cut: all four items are true against my manual — the cell (display 3, green light) contains exactly one instruction, cut the green wire, with no conditions, no sequence, no second step; the green wire is position 3 (blue, yellow, green left to right); and the double report from Deaf's eyes and Blind's fingers agrees on every detail, including no other modules on the casing. So I give exactly the requested confirmation: four thumbs up, four thumbs up again, three fists for wire 3, one fist for exactly one cut. I will not append anything else — Blind specified "exactly," and an extra symbol risks a misread hold. On the display-change question: Deaf already reported the 3 as static between checks and sees the bomb every round, so any change reaching Deaf's eyes gets spoken to us next round and I can re-check the table then; no gesture code exists to ask more finely, and inventing one now would only add noise at the moment of the cut.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "✊", "✊", "✊", "✊"])
```
